newsitem.title: ESTONIA: PENNU TO MOVE TO DEALER MARKET.
newsitem.headline: PENNU TO MOVE TO DEALER MARKET.

text.p: Trading in shares for computer maker Pennu will be changed from public a order book to the dealer market from Monday, the Tallinn bourse said on Friday.
"A sustainable number of active recognised dealers have emerged," Rain Semper, the listing manager with the bourse, told Reuters.
Recognised dealers for Pennu shares are Innovatsioonipank, Forekspank , Hansapank and Cresco, the stock exchange said.
The minimum amount for Pennu shares is 500 shares and the is spread 0.05 kroons, it added in a statement.
The dealer market is based on recognised dealers, who have an obligation to give bids and offer quotations on a continual basis.

The public order book is a trading model for shares with less liquidity, which have one or ni recognized dealers. All dealers have the right to enter bids and offer quatations, but they are not obliged to do so.
Pennu shares moved from the dealer market to the public order book trading system on January 2.
